patches.purpose: Use warning options that are valid under MSVC/clang-cl builds of ultramodern.
Use warning options that are valid under MSVC/clang-cl builds of librecomp.
Ignore unregistered/null hardware event queues during early Rocket startup.
Wake blocked external-message waiters when the host runtime quits.
Prevent the emulated scheduler from cascading into another guest thread after shutdown begins.
Delay graphics SP completion until the renderer has consumed task inputs; superseded safely by the following RDRAM snapshot patch.
Snapshot 8 MiB RDRAM for queued graphics tasks so RT64 parses immutable task data.
Coalesce pending VI screen updates so graphics tasks are not starved by stale presents.
Restore original early SP completion now that graphics tasks own immutable RDRAM snapshots.
Yield between SP and DP completion to preserve independent hardware-event ordering.
Expose host-modelled N64 AI DMA busy/full status so Rocket's original n_audio manager preserves hardware FIFO pacing.
Use the Linux prctl thread-name path on Android/Bionic so ultramodern links on ARM64 Android.
Separate mod profiles and saves from ROM storage; protect built-in game fixes against hooks and forced replacements; synchronize patched instruction caches.
Reuse immutable 8 MiB task snapshot leases without redundant initialization, retaining SP/DP ordering and bounding idle cached buffers.
Recognize KSEG0 entrypoints, apply configured entry-function sizes before renaming, preserve real ELF sizes, and keep the configured VRAM authoritative over the ROM-0x1000 fallback.
Carry DKR-R's RT64 interpolation-target approval for freshly modified framebuffers.
Expose a monotonic count of successful interpolated presentations for runtime validation.
Bind early presents to the exact workload framebuffer set so alternating Rocket buffers cannot race interpolation selection.
Preapprove the exact PresentEarly framebuffer before asynchronous RT64 workload rendering.
Allow the approved interpolation target to be created by the same workload instead of requiring a stale prior framebuffer.
Zoom Rocket's authored 18x14 overscan-safe border out only at final VI presentation so 4:3 and Expand fill their intended viewport without changing guest rendering or timing.

Keep shader embedding tools on the build host during cross-compilation, wire SDL2/Plume for Android, stub unused RT64 native file dialogs on Android, and use SDL_Vulkan_GetDrawableSize for Ubuntu 22.04 SDL2 compatibility.

Rocket-R global interpolation stability v5: carry RenderEntry semantic owners only across adjacent authored frames with mutual unambiguous continuity, bind exact FIFO task sidecars, and explicitly use G_EX_ID_IGNORE for ambiguous, conflicting or unrecognised model matrices so RT64 never falls back to anonymous transform matching. Rocket-R v33 additionally gives only the pre-world sky/background display-list subtree a task-owned semantic interpolation group, including topology-safe dynamic vertex interpolation.

Expose Rocket-R launcher control over the original N64 Bayer colour dithering by forcing decoded RT64 draw-state RGB/alpha dither modes to disabled while the option is off, without mutating guest RDP state.
Port DKR-R's proven configurable RT64 sampler anisotropy control so Rocket-R can select 1x-16x before sampler creation.
Port DKR-R's live mip LOD bias path through RT64 raster parameters and texture sampling without rebuilding samplers.
Add Rocket-R renderer-owned fog-distance, decal z-fighting tolerance, and presentation-only HUD aspect/scale/safe-area controls.
Add Rocket-R final-VI clean filtering, debanding, scanline/CRT post-processing and monotonic presentation telemetry.
Add optional precompiled custom final-VI pixel shaders using RT64's existing fullscreen vertex shader, descriptor contract and backend-specific DXIL/SPIR-V binaries.
Preserve constant angular progress in quaternion interpolation and rigid shape on the first matched frame; snap invalid decompositions.
Restore component interpolation for singular shadow projections while retaining V45 rigid rotation and first-match fixes.
Make Android native-window guards, zstd qsort fallback and Python shader embedding compatibility reproducible through the checked dependency pipeline, replacing temporary build-time rewrites.
Add live Original-to-Highest texture-distance detail control for native N64 mip tile selection and replacement texture mipmaps.
Use Android RGBA swapchain and matching VI pipelines; constrain mobile replacement-texture memory for the 3 GB phone target.
Retain and replace Android native Vulkan surfaces at the present-thread resize boundary after background/resume.
Preserve proven sky presentation identities, validate vertex connectivity, interpolate scrolling tiles across wraps, and expose live texture-space sky dithering reduction.
Tag the retail camera-scrolled sky rectangle, apply texture-space dithering reduction, and interpolate its guarded source rows at presentation rate.
Interpolate the proven player wheel rotation, scale and shear together; retain conservative handling of all other matrices.
Remove repeating dither phases during sky scrolling with a complete texture-space filter; retain alpha and strong edges.
Recompile raster shaders when sky filtering or shared raster parameters change in an incremental build.
Average the entire eight-column sky gradient so full dithering reduction is independent of texture sampling phase.
Filter the verified narrow sky in a cached native-size RGBA texture; remove sixteen per-pixel filter samples while preserving fractional scrolling and replacement packs.
Route Rocket's raw 1024-row sky declaration through the cached 256-row native filter while preserving physical TMEM wrapping and replacement packs.
Flush CPU uploads and invalidate readbacks for non-coherent Vulkan memory; share resources across distinct queue families and report Android memory capabilities.
Give Android shader compilation threads a real background nice priority without changing foreground rendering or audio scheduling.
Record Android Vulkan device, driver and API versions once at startup for device-specific graphics reports.
